source: https://github.com/IBMa/equal-access, folder accessibility-checker-engine/src/v4/rules/ (rule files), accessibility-checker-engine/src/v4/api/IRule.ts and IGuideline.ts (enums), accessibility-checker-engine/src/v4/rulesets.ts + sc-urls.json (guideline checkpoint lists), accessibility-checker-engine/src/v4/checker/Checker.ts and common/module/src/report/ReporterManager.ts (level logic)
method: A Python script read every *.ts file in src/v4/rules as text (no repository code was executed): it stripped comments, parsed each `export const <name>: Rule = {` object's data keys (id, context, rulesets, act, messages, refactor, dependencies) with a small tokenizer and recursive-descent parser that skips the `run` function, and collected the RulePass/RuleFail/RulePotential/RuleManual calls and their literal reason ids from the function body to get the eRuleConfidence values each rule can return. Reported outcomes were then derived per guideline by reproducing Checker.getReasonLevel (ruleset level per reason code, using the guideline checkpoint lists built from rulesets.ts and sc-urls.json) and the checker package's ReporterManager.valueToLevel (level + confidence -> VIOLATION, POTENTIAL_VIOLATION, MANUAL, RECOMMENDATION, POTENTIAL_RECOMMENDATION, PASS).
caveats: The engine's own enum eRuleConfidence has the values PASS, FAIL, POTENTIAL and MANUAL (src/v4/api/IRule.ts); the ruleset `level` is eRulePolicy (VIOLATION, RECOMMENDATION, INFORMATION). The `outcomes` vocabulary (VIOLATION, POTENTIAL_VIOLATION, MANUAL, RECOMMENDATION, POTENTIAL_RECOMMENDATION, PASS, INFORMATION) is the combination of the two, as the accessibility-checker package reports it; `confidences` and `reason_ids` keep the raw enum values.

For a rule in the WCAG_2_2 ruleset, `level`, `toolkit_level` and `outcomes` are the values for a run with only WCAG_2_2 selected; `level_by_ruleset` and `outcomes_by_ruleset` give the other rulesets. Rules whose level differs between rulesets (VIOLATION in IBM_Accessibility, RECOMMENDATION in the WCAG rulesets): aria_content_in_landmark, aria_landmark_name_unique, element_tabbable_role_valid, style_highcontrast_visible.

11 rules are inactive (`active: false`, `outcomes: []`): they are exported by the engine but belong to no active guideline, so Checker.check() never runs them. Causes: `rulesets: []` (aria_graphic_labelled, aria_img_labelled, asciiart_alt_exists, element_scrollable_tabbable, emoticons_alt_exists, form_submit_review, input_placeholder_label_visible); ruleset `id: []` with a comment that the rule was turned off (aria_search_label_unique, meta_redirect_optional, style_before_after_review); the DEBUG ruleset is commented out in rulesets.ts (debug_paths).

Two active rules (aria_accessiblename_exists, img_alt_null) have one reason code mapped only to the IBM-only checkpoint 'ARIA'; in a WCAG-only run the Checker reports that reason code with policy INFORMATION (outcome 'INFORMATION'), which the accessibility-checker package gives no report level and so does not count.

Every result call uses a literal reason id (no dynamic ids were found). Commented-out calls were excluded; the comment stripper was checked by comparing call counts before and after stripping (6 files differ, all because of commented-out calls, listed in diagnostics.call_count_differences).
debug_paths has no result call (its run() returns null); detector_tabbable (EXTENSIONS ruleset, level INFORMATION) only returns PASS. Both support the browser extension and test no WCAG requirement.

`criteria` lists the WCAG success-criterion numbers of ruleset entries that name at least one ruleset; the non-WCAG checkpoints 'ARIA' and 'HTML' (IBM rulesets) and '1' (EXTENSIONS/DEBUG) are in `other_checkpoints`. The engine's WCAG_2_2 checkpoint list still contains the obsolete 4.1.1 (no rule maps to it).
`act` lists the ACT rule ids found as plain strings and as keys of per-reason mapping objects; the per-reason pass/fail/cantTell/inapplicable mapping itself is not reproduced.
The meaning of the IBM toolkit levels (LEVEL_ONE to LEVEL_FOUR) is not defined in the repository; only the enum values 1-4 are.
Message keys with no matching result call exist in 4 rules (aria_graphic_labelled, aria_img_labelled, debug_paths, form_submit_review); they were ignored for outcomes.

levels_explained.VIOLATION: Ruleset level (eRulePolicy.VIOLATION in src/v4/api/IRule.ts): failing this rule breaks the requirement; with a FAIL confidence the tools report a 'Violation', with POTENTIAL or MANUAL they report 'Needs review'.
levels_explained.RECOMMENDATION: Ruleset level (eRulePolicy.RECOMMENDATION): the tools report the issue as a 'Recommendation' whatever the confidence (FAIL, POTENTIAL or MANUAL).
levels_explained.INFORMATION: Ruleset level (eRulePolicy.INFORMATION): informational only; used by the EXTENSIONS/DEBUG rules. The Checker also assigns this level when a result's reason code matches none of the rule's reasonCodes-restricted ruleset entries.
levels_explained.LEVEL_ONE: eToolkitLevel.LEVEL_ONE = "1" (src/v4/api/IGuideline.ts): IBM Equal Access Toolkit priority level 1, the highest priority. The repository does not define the levels further.
levels_explained.LEVEL_FOUR: eToolkitLevel.LEVEL_FOUR = "4": toolkit priority level 4, the lowest priority.
levels_explained.FAIL: eRuleConfidence.FAIL, returned by RuleFail(): the engine detected a definite failure automatically.
levels_explained.POTENTIAL: eRuleConfidence.POTENTIAL, returned by RulePotential(): the engine found a likely problem that a person must confirm (ACT outcome cantTell).
levels_explained.MANUAL: eRuleConfidence.MANUAL, returned by RuleManual(): the engine cannot test this; it always asks for a manual check (ACT outcome cantTell).
levels_explained.PASS: eRuleConfidence.PASS, returned by RulePass(): the element passed the rule.
levels_explained.outcome:VIOLATION: Rule level VIOLATION + confidence FAIL: an automatic failure, reported as 'Violation' (eRuleLevel.violation in the accessibility-checker package; counted as a failure by default).
levels_explained.outcome:POTENTIAL_VIOLATION: Rule level VIOLATION + confidence POTENTIAL: reported as 'Needs review' (eRuleLevel.potentialviolation; also counted as a failure by the accessibility-checker default failLevels).
levels_explained.outcome:MANUAL: Rule level VIOLATION or RECOMMENDATION + confidence MANUAL: reported as 'Needs review' (eRuleLevel.manual); a person must check.
levels_explained.outcome:RECOMMENDATION: Rule level RECOMMENDATION + confidence FAIL: reported as 'Recommendation' (eRuleLevel.recommendation); not counted as a failure.
levels_explained.outcome:POTENTIAL_RECOMMENDATION: Rule level RECOMMENDATION + confidence POTENTIAL: reported as 'Recommendation' (eRuleLevel.potentialrecommendation); not counted as a failure.
levels_explained.outcome:INFORMATION: Rule level INFORMATION + a non-PASS confidence: the accessibility-checker package gives it no report level; in practice only for EXTENSIONS/DEBUG rules or reason codes outside a rule's reasonCodes-restricted ruleset entries.

rulesets_explained.WCAG_2_2: WCAG 2.2 (A, AA): all level A and AA success criteria of WCAG 2.0, 2.1 and 2.2 (56 checkpoints).
rulesets_explained.WCAG_2_1: WCAG 2.1 (A, AA): all level A and AA success criteria of WCAG 2.0 and 2.1 (50 checkpoints).
rulesets_explained.WCAG_2_0: WCAG 2.0 (A, AA): all level A and AA success criteria of WCAG 2.0 (38 checkpoints).
rulesets_explained.IBM_Accessibility: IBM Accessibility 7.3: the WCAG_2_2 checkpoints plus the IBM supplemental checkpoints 'ARIA' and 'HTML' (58 checkpoints).
rulesets_explained.IBM_Accessibility_next: IBM Accessibility next: same checkpoint list as IBM_Accessibility; used to stage rules for the next IBM ruleset version.
rulesets_explained.EXTENSIONS: Extension Rules: checkpoint '1' only; rules that support the browser extension (not accessibility requirements).
rulesets_explained.DEBUG: Debug ruleset: its definition is commented out in rulesets.ts, so rules that only list DEBUG never run through the Checker.
